description: ABUSIVE-DYNAMICS N2 -- ISOLATION AS AN ACTIVE PROCESS (support edges severed over time), block 301000. Maps ABUSIVE_RELATIONSHIPS_NETWORK.md's A3 + B3 / Part E N2. Composes N1's credibility-asymmetry loop (abusive_n1_credibility_loop, block 298000, UNMODIFIED -- riding snap_frustration/arousal_window_coreg in turn, UNMODIFIED) with TWO new, independent, coupled severing drivers over a small population of NetworkNode 'support nodes', each holding one support_edge to the victim: (1) n2_abuser_active_sever -- the abuser's own active isolation tactic, a mechanical per-node severing SCHEDULE (sever_at_tick, set once at construction) acted on by the rule only when the arm's isolation_tactic_on switch is armed; (2) n2_network_drift_sever -- the network drifting away ON ITS OWN, pulled by the SAME belief_gap N1's own n1_network_credibility_stated rule already computes (never recomputed here) once it crosses that node's pre-assigned (staggered) drift_threshold. Both rules del_edge the SAME support_edge; a node severed by either driver cannot fire either rule again (match requires the edge to still exist). NO reward/punishment anywhere. NO Rust, NO new Term (Gte is the only Term new to this line, already a peer of Eq/Lt/Gt in the engine). self_load_only, default-OFF.

microtheory.name: isolation_as_active_process
microtheory.description: Isolation is not a trait of the victim or a failure of her friends -- it is DOUBLY driven, by two independent, coupled mechanisms that happen to share one graph quantity (the support_edge count). The abuser's active severing tactic acts on a schedule regardless of what the network believes; the network's own drift acts on what N1's credibility loop has already corrupted, independent of anything the abuser directly does to that edge. Neither driver needs the other to operate; together they are strictly worse than either alone, which is the measured content of 'doubly driven.'
